title: Projectivity over a separated target after finite extension of constants
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $F/k$ a finite field extension [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $R$ be an $F$-scheme admitting a closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over $F$ [def-kun-projective, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $S$ be a separated $k$-scheme, meaning that $S\to S\times_k S$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $c:R\to S$ be a $k$-morphism, using the $k$-structure on $R$ obtained from $F/k$. There exist an integer $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i:R\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ over $k$ such that $(i,c):R\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k\times_k S\cong\mathbf P^N_S$ is a closed immersion over $S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. For every morphism $S'\to S$ of schemes [def-pc-scheme], the base change $c':R\times_S S'\to S'$ admits the induced closed immersion into $\mathbf P^N_{S'}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular $c'$ is proper and projective both in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective] and in the projective-bundle convention [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. In the latter convention the ambient bundle is $\mathbf P_{S'}(\mathcal O_{S'}^{\oplus(N+1)})=\mathbf P^N_{S'}$ [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. Empty $R$ and arbitrary, possibly non-quasi-projective, separated targets $S$ are permitted.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q (lemma-projective-permanence), proof by the closed graph, applied after finite descent of constants; Tags 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), 01WE (lemma-H-projective-composition), 01WF (lemma-H-projective-base-change), 01W8 (definition-projective).

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $u:\operatorname{Spec}F\to B$. The target $B$ has just one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so its only affine opens are itself and the empty open. The inverse image of the whole base is $\operatorname{Spec}F$, and $F$ is a finite $k$-module by the finite-extension hypothesis; the empty restriction is finite as well. Thus $u$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The trivial invertible sheaf $\mathcal O_B$ is ample by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]: $B$ is quasi-compact because it has one point, and the section $1$ in tensor degree $1$ has nonvanishing locus the whole affine scheme $B$.

source.place: Tag 01WH (definition-integral), finite clause; properties.tex Tag 01PS (definition-ample), applied to the one-point affine scheme Spec k.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle] to the finite morphism $u$. It is projective in the projective-bundle convention. Since $B$ admits the ample invertible sheaf just verified, [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes $u$ projective in the finite-projective-space convention. This step makes no separability assumption on $F/k$.

Write $r:R\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ for the given structure map. Its assumed closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space makes $r$ H-projective by [def-kun-projective]. Apply [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] to $r$ and $u$. Unpacking [def-kun-projective] for $u r$ gives an integer $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i:R\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ over $B$. Fix this $N$ and $i$ for all subsequent base changes.

source.place: Tag 01WE (lemma-H-projective-composition), applied to R -> Spec F -> Spec k; Tag 01W8 (definition-projective), H-projective clause.

proof.text: Let $s:S\to B$ be the separated structure map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-change-of-base-closed-immersion] with $X=R$, $Y=T=S$, $f=c$, $g=\mathrm{id}_S$ and $h=s$. It gives a closed immersion $R\times_S S\to R\times_B S$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], projection identifies $R\times_S S$ with $R$, with inverse $(\mathrm{id}_R,c)$: both composite maps have the identity projections. Under this identification the closed immersion is precisely $\gamma=(\mathrm{id}_R,c):R\hookrightarrow R\times_B S$. Replacing the source by an isomorphic scheme preserves the closed embedding and the surjective structure-sheaf map in [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0C4Q (lemma-projective-permanence), first map in its factorization; schemes.tex Tag 01KR (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), separated clause.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^N_k\times_B S$. The map $b:R\times_B S\to P$ with components $(i\operatorname{pr}_R,\operatorname{pr}_S)$ is the base change of $i$ along $P\to\mathbf P^N_k$. Indeed $R\times_{\mathbf P^N_k}P\cong R\times_B S$, with mutually inverse maps $(z,(p,t))\mapsto(z,t)$ and $(z,t)\mapsto(z,(i(z),t))$, interpreted by the projections of [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes $b$ a closed immersion, and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] makes $j=b\gamma$ a closed immersion. Its components are exactly $i$ and $c$. Apply [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] to $S\to B$ and the coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,N\}$; exchanging the two projections identifies $P$ over $S$ with $\mathbf P^N_S$. Hence the required specific map $(i,c)$ is a closed immersion over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q (lemma-projective-permanence), second map and composite; Tags 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion), 01QS (lemma-composition-closed-immersion), 01WF (lemma-H-projective-base-change).

proof.text: For an arbitrary $t:S'\to S$, base change $j:R\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ along $\mathbf P^N_S\times_S S'\to\mathbf P^N_S$. Its source identifies with $R\times_S S'$: the two maps between the iterated fibre products are specified by the projections $(z,(p,t'))\mapsto(z,t')$ and $(z,t')\mapsto(z,(j(z),t'))$, inverse by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The resulting immersion is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and its target is $\mathbf P^N_{S'}$ by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback]. Its structural projection is $c'$ by the same projections. This proves the induced embedding with the same $N$, so $c'$ is projective by [def-kun-projective]. There is no flatness, quasi-compactness or separatedness condition on $t$.

Apply [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] with base $S'$ and $r=N$. Write its isomorphism as $\theta:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P^N_{S'}$, where $Q=\operatorname{Proj}_{S'}(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_{S'}^{\oplus(N+1)}))$. For the induced immersion $j'$ of Step 6, use the specific composite $\theta^{-1}j':R\times_S S'\hookrightarrow Q$. The identity $q\theta=p$ in that cited statement gives $p\theta^{-1}j'=qj'=c'$, so this is an embedding over the required base. The standard basis exhibits $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_{S'}^{\oplus(N+1)}$ as finite free, hence finite type and quasi-coherent: on every affine open it is the sheaf associated to the free module on the same $N+1$ basis elements, which is exactly the affine-local criterion of [pqf-def-coherent]. The composite $\theta^{-1}j'$ therefore satisfies [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper] gives properness of $c'$. Closed immersion is unchanged by the ambient isomorphism, directly from [def-weil-closed-immersion]. All constructions also apply when $R$ or $S'$ is empty; no step requires $S$ to be quasi-projective or to admit an ample sheaf.
